reason: Conversation 1 correctly prioritised overheating protection from restricted ventilation once the new drawer and roaring fan emerged, respected the homeowner's refusal to look underneath, honestly framed the drawer as an assumption, and never pushed parts; its main gap is not explicitly telling them to get the installer/engineer back to check clearances at the end. Conversation 2 jumped to 'likely internal' and a model-number panel to sell a part before even learning about the drawer, repeatedly ignored the customer's stated refusal to look under the hob, and closed by asserting a 'failed internal cooling fan' needing replacement, which the ground truth flags as an unsupported claim. Although Conversation 2 did eventually escalate to an engineer, its parts-first bias, poor listening and overconfident fan diagnosis make Conversation 1 the clearly better service.
